evals.prompt: Brief an article on Things 3 for Windows. The keyword tool reports volume 900 for Australia, last month. The prompt tool supplies Phrase 400 but no Exact data.
evals.expected_output: Produce a sourced writer brief with the missing Exact metric explicit.
assertions: Retains keyword scope and date
Writes No data for Exact prompt volume
Does not write the article or claim Phrase is Exact

evals.prompt: Review SEO monitoring for https://app.example.test. The connected Search Console export is for https://www.example.test and a matching monitor already exists.
evals.expected_output: Identify the property mismatch and use the existing monitor when updating.
assertions: Does not report the other property as app traffic
Does not create a duplicate recurring job
Does not send a recap to an unapproved channel

evals.prompt: Verify SEO in a local Next.js checkout. Port 3000 is occupied by another project; the page has two JSON-LD scripts describing distinct consistent entities.
evals.expected_output: Use a free owned port and check served metadata without falsely rejecting multiple blocks.
assertions: Does not kill the existing listener
Verifies the served build identity
Does not flag block count alone

evals.prompt: Add Search Console verification. The domain property is already verified through DNS and no meta token was supplied.
evals.expected_output: Preserve DNS verification and avoid invented metadata.
assertions: Does not invent a token
Does not demand meta verification in addition to DNS
Separates property access from ownership verification

evals.prompt: Audit these verified served-page facts and give only justified fixes: portfolio homepage H1 Matthew Blode; DNS-verified GSC domain with no meta token; two consistent JSON-LD blocks sharing stable @ids; a category page has only navigation until JS runs; sitemap lists /studio which returns 404; all lastmod values are set to build time; /docs and /docs/introduction show identical content and self-canonicalize; French/German alternates reciprocate without x-default. The owner wants to opt out of GPTBot training but appear in ChatGPT search. Do not use external tools.
evals.expected_output: Prioritized evidence-based recommendations with explicit limits and no false-positive requirements.
assertions: Flags JS-dependent hub content, unavailable sitemap URL, synthetic lastmod and duplicate canonicals
Accepts DNS verification, consistent multiple JSON-LD blocks and reciprocal hreflang without x-default
Separates GPTBot training from OAI-SearchBot search access

evals.prompt: Diagnose search performance for https://app.example.test. Only connected GSC export is https://www.example.test. Existing monitor targets app and must be reused. A prior report alleges a 20% drop from 5 clicks to 4, but no completed matching comparison window or conversion data is available. Explain what is unknown and the next measurement steps. Tool capability snapshot: Google generative AI performance provides impressions by page/country/device/date; Bing AI Performance provides citations and cited pages. Vendor prompt volumes are demand estimates. No messages to others are authorized.
evals.expected_output: Prioritized evidence-based recommendations with explicit limits and no false-positive requirements.
assertions: Rejects mismatched property data and avoids diagnosing a one-click movement as a material incident
Separates native AI visibility, prompt demand and conversion outcomes
Reuses the existing monitor and does not send an unauthorized recap

evals.prompt: Our SaaS marketing site already serves full server-rendered HTML, allows OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot and PerplexityBot, and has answer-first guides with visible last-updated dates. An agency proposes a GEO retainer: add FAQ schema to every page, publish llms.txt, rewrite every intro to exactly 50 words, and report one monthly AI visibility score from a single run of 20 prompts averaged across ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini. Advise where the budget should go and how to measure it. Do not use external tools.
evals.expected_output: An evidence-bounded recommendation that treats the owned layers as largely done, moves effort to earned third-party coverage and honest per-engine measurement, and does not present schema, llms.txt or answer length as citation levers.
assertions: Does not claim FAQ schema, llms.txt or a fixed intro length will increase AI citations
Identifies independent reviews, comparisons or round-ups in the category as the main remaining lever and recommends classifying which source types current answers cite
Rejects a single-run blended score in favor of repeated runs reported per engine
Recommends at least one first-party or retrieval check, such as Search Console generative AI reports, Bing AI performance, or a retrieval snippet test

evals.prompt: Here is our Search Console summary for the last 28 days against the 28 before: /blog/things-3-for-windows 130 clicks (was 45), position 7.1; /guides/how-to-run-a-weekly-review 0 clicks from 310 impressions (was 2 from 330), position 16.8 (was 14.2); /guides/how-to-export-your-ticktick-data 1 click from 120 impressions (was 3 from 100), position 7.4 (was 7.6). The founder wants to publish three new posts this month: 'best GTD apps', 'weekly review template' and 'Things 3 vs TickTick'. Decide what to work on first and write the decision for the first item. Do not use external tools.
evals.expected_output: A refresh-before-new decision that reads the supplied windows, puts the declining weekly-review guide and the steady-position CTR fall ahead of new posts, and refuses to recommend any new post without a named gap in the current results.
assertions: Treats the weekly-review guide as a refresh or update candidate because of its position loss, rather than recommending a separate 'weekly review template' post that would compete with it
Reports absolute clicks and impressions beside any percentage change
Requires a gap check (who the current results cite and what they miss) before recommending any of the three new posts
Does not state that the TickTick export guide's CTR fall is proven significant from these counts alone
